children: For much of the FY23 and FY25 period, investors questioned if Laurus Labs’ relentless spending on new manufacturing blocks, research programmes and emerging technologies would ever generate adequate returns.
Today, those investments are beginning to pay off.

Shares of the Hyderabad-based active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) and Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisation company have nearly doubled over the past year as a surge in CDMO orders, particularly from late-stage and commercial products, has transformed its earnings profile and restored investor confidence.
The rally accelerated after FY26 and Q1 FY27 results, taking the stock into the Rs 1 lakh crore market-capitalisation club.

Revenue from the CDMO business jumped 70 percent year-on-year to Rs 835 crore in the June quarter, accounting for 41 percent of overall revenue, while consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to 31.5 percent from 24.3 percent a year ago.

The turnaround comes after a prolonged investment cycle. Laurus has spent more than Rs 4,700 crore on capex between FY22 and FY27, with about 83 percent directed toward API and CDMO businesses. It has also stepped up investments in peptides, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), gene therapies and biologics capabilities, areas that weighed on profitability during the downcycle.
Customer wins validate the strategy
Those bets are now translating into customer wins.

"Even during those lean years, we have said that the decisions we took will take time to reflect; in pharma it takes about 18-24 months to see results of the investments," a senior executive of the company told Moneycontrol on condition of anonymity.

The company continued investing despite the weak environment in 2023-2025 because large innovator clients preferred partners with ready infrastructure and the ability to support programmes through commercialisation.

Laurus reported that 55 percent of CDMO revenue in the June quarter came from commercial supplies, while the remainder was largely from Phase III projects that could convert into commercial opportunities in the coming years
The executive added that the CDMO run-rate was supported by multiple customers and products and not a single large order, providing better visibility than in previous growth spurts.
Fresh capex signals confidence
The company is confident enough to increase FY27 capex guidance to Rs 2,000 crore from the earlier Rs 1,000-1,500 crore range.

In the recent earnings call, management told analysts that the new investments are linked to identified customer demand across human health and animal health programmes and are meant for multiple products rather than speculative expansion.

Founder and CEO Satyanarayana Chava said additional investments are being undertaken to meet capacity requirements from existing customers. "This capex, unlike earlier capex, what we have done, this we are doing for a purpose, for a product and capacity what is needed in the near term for our partners' needs," Chava said.
Brokerages see long growth runway
Brokerages see the spending cycle turning into a growth engine.

ICICI Securities said Laurus has consistently pursued growth capex even during periods of earnings weakness, with benefits typically emerging after a lag of two to three years. The brokerage highlighted that CDMO quarterly revenue has risen from about Rs 220-250 crore two years ago to nearly Rs 835 crore now, while reiterating management’s target of CDMO contributing more than half of company revenue by FY30.

InCred Research upgraded the stock after the June quarter results, saying commercial CDMO supplies had materially improved visibility on earnings growth. It expects the business mix to shift decisively toward higher-margin CDMO operations, helping EBITDA margins approach 30 percent over the next two years.
Laurus is not slowing investments despite the ongoing recovery.

Research and development expenditure rose to 5.8 percent of the revenue in Q1, up roughly 70 percent year-on-year, as the company invested in gene therapy platforms, antibody drug conjudgate (ADC) infrastructure and complex product pipelines. The company has also expanded its peptide capabilities and continues to invest in advanced biologics, areas management believes represent the next wave of outsourced pharmaceutical manufacturing. The growth beyond 2030 depends on building capabilities today.

title: Laurus Labs’ years-long capex gamble pays off as CDMO orders drive earnings, stock surge
